name: Presence API
author: WordPress.org

sections.description:
Presence API gives WordPress a system-wide awareness layer. It tracks which users are logged in, which admin screen they are on, and which posts they are editing.

Data flows through the Heartbeat API and is stored in a dedicated wp_presence table with a 150-second TTL. No writes to wp_postmeta means no post-cache invalidation on every heartbeat.

On a multisite network, Network Admin gets its own view of the same data: a Who’s Online dashboard widget listing the busiest sites and who is on each, an Online column in the Sites list, and an Online view, filter, and column in the Users list. These require the manage_network capability.

Features

  • Admin bar indicator showing who’s online and who’s on this page
  • Active Posts dashboard widget grouped by post
  • Editors column in the post list
  • Online filter in the Users list

For Developers

PHP functions, REST endpoints, WP-CLI commands, filters, and room conventions are documented in the GitHub repository.

Background

A feature plugin sponsored by the WordPress Core team, exploring what system-wide presence could look like for a future WordPress release. Follow development on make.wordpress.org/core with the tag #presence-api.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for “Presence API”, then click Install Now.
  2. Activate through the Plugins menu.

Or install manually:

  1. Download the zip and upload the presence-api folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate through the Plugins menu.
sections.faq:
Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Network-activate it and Network Admin gains a Who’s Online dashboard widget listing the busiest sites and who is on each, an Online column in the Sites list, and an Online view, filter, and column in the Users list. Every site keeps its own widgets and lists, counting only the people on that site.

Who can see network-wide presence?

Anyone with the manage_network capability, which on a default network means super admins. The wp_presence_network_capability filter changes what is required.

Can a site stop recording presence?

Yes. Clear the Presence checkbox on Settings > General, or run wp presence recording set off. Every screen empties within one TTL as the rows already stored expire. On multisite, Network Admin > Settings has the same checkbox for every site at once; whichever switch is off decides.

For code, the wp_presence_recording_enabled and wp_presence_network_recording_enabled filters take the checkboxes as their defaults, so a filter always has the last word.
sections.changelog:
Only the most recent releases are listed here. For the full history, see https://github.com/WordPress/presence-api/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

0.10.0

  • Fold shared screens into one row in the admin bar menu (#615).
  • List people editing posts first in the admin bar menu (#603).
  • Refresh the Editors column on each heartbeat (#606).
  • Refresh the Online users list on each heartbeat (#604).
  • Show the stale-screen banner on Settings API, Privacy and Network Admin screens (#619).
  • Bump the right Users screen on a row Remove and skip bumps while deleting a site (#628).
  • Link admin bar rows to the comment, user or term being edited (#617).
  • Link Network Admin rows and count the network in the admin bar (#618).
  • Read the network Online view from the heartbeat’s screen (#622).
  • Refresh presence rows on SQLite with CASE instead of IF() (#623).
  • Cut e2e runtime with backdated fixtures and readiness waits (#621).

0.9.0

  • Gate where people are behind a per-user view_presence_location meta cap (#571).
  • Give each user a room-assigned color from Gutenberg’s palette (#574).
  • Keep the admin bar presence node in sync on each heartbeat (#589).
  • Put people on this page first in the admin bar menu and link everyone else to where they are (#597).
  • Retire the site Who’s Online dashboard widget (#591).
  • Ring each admin bar face in its block editor collaborator color.
  • Say how many people the admin bar menu leaves out (#594).
  • Seat the admin bar faces beside My Account and build the menu from core groups (#565).
  • Show whole faces in the admin bar and beside each name in its menu.
  • Carry the filter nonce on the Plugins screen’s online users link (#569).
  • Close the remaining location leaks and refresh the screen token (#600).
  • Keep post locks in the presence table instead of post meta (#551).
  • Keep presence markup and location to the people allowed them (#596).
  • List everyone online in the admin bar and keep only their location behind the cap (#590).
  • Skip an unchanged editor tick’s presence write (#553).
  • Store the recording option so reading it costs no query (#552).

0.8.0

  • Add wp_presence_exchange() and wp_presence_leave() (#546).
  • Say when Heartbeat cannot keep presence current (#544).

0.7.0

  • Filter wp_get_presence() by client_id prefix in SQL (#530).
  • Store an expiry per presence row (#541).
  • Stop the site TTL filter overriding an explicit $timeout (#540).
  • Typos CI failure caused by changelog link label in readme.txt (#527).
  • Decide redundant presence writes inside the upsert (#542).

0.6.0

  • Add Network Admin plugin action links (#513).
  • Add wp_presence_is_available() for integrators (#519).
  • Expose the room’s collaborator count as JS hooks (#503).
  • Centralize network site status filtering (#453).
  • Keep a client that is still pinging out of the idle state (#522).
  • Keep the collaboration edge state in the presence table (#514).
